comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA study programme, checked 2026-09-26; 2026–27 study guide confirms the degree identity and load
comparator.sourceNotes: The published three-year curriculum is 60+60+60=180 EC: ten first-year 6-EC courses; ten second-year 6-EC courses; in year three three taught 6-EC courses, 30 EC genuine free choice and a compulsory 12-EC thesis. The Greek and Latin language-acquisition, original-text reading and linguistic/literary-analysis sequence is compulsory; the 30-EC choice space is left open. The programme page contains a stray joint-degree paragraph referring to Oudheidwetenschappen, a different programme. The named GLTC curriculum and its 2026–27 study-guide entry establish the target as the UvA Greek and Latin Language and Culture bachelor; that unrelated paragraph is not treated as its degree identity.

exception.reason: The compulsory curriculum centers on progressive acquisition and advanced reading of Ancient Greek and Latin, original-language epic, tragedy, historiography and lyric, Greek and Latin linguistics, and a thesis in the field. UCR has relevant ancient-world and literary-cultural courses but no Greek or Latin language instruction or philological sequence. A 24-course archaeology, heritage, philosophy and world-literature path would be a different ancient-cultures degree, not a defensible Greek and Latin Language and Culture response. The open 30 EC cannot repair the missing compulsory core.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected generic published route totals 180 EC: year one 60 EC compulsory (including Greek 1, Latin 1 and two further Greek/Latin language-and-reading courses); year two 60 EC compulsory (including original-language epic and linguistics in both languages); year three 18 EC taught, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC subject thesis. No minor or elective is fabricated.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed the 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including actual descriptions, outline profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology and MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology cover ancient material culture; MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy treats Athenian civic heritage; MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature discusses Homer and Virgil alongside other traditions; MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy and MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean offer adjacent historical, philosophical or literary context. These support ancient-world inquiry, but none teaches Ancient Greek or Latin grammar, translation, close reading in the original languages, or a progressive classical philology sequence. Communications courses such as MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning address language in other contexts and cannot substitute. Even a coherent archaeology-and-literature 24-course plan would miss the external degree’s defining language core.
